title: I bought a used couch online for twenty dollars. The seller made me promise never to look under the cushions.
transcript:
I bought a used couch online for twenty dollars. The seller made me promise never to look under the cushions. The seller was an older woman who wouldn't come outside. She slid the cash envelope back under the door and said through the wood, "Just don't lift the cushions. Promise me."

I promised. It was twenty dollars. I didn't care.

For the first week it was the most comfortable couch I'd ever owned. I fell asleep on it every night with the television on.

Then I started waking up in different spots. The left end, the right end, once on the floor beside it, my blanket folded neatly on the armrest. I never fold anything.

On Sunday I dropped my keys between the cushions, and without thinking I lifted one up.

The fabric underneath was covered in handwriting. Names, dozens of them, in different pens, each one crossed out with a single straight line. Some were faded almost to nothing.

The last name near the bottom was the seller's. Crossed out, the ink still dark.

Under hers, in fresh ink, in my own handwriting, was my name.

Not crossed out yet.

I put the cushion back. I tried to drag the couch to the curb, but it wouldn't move.

And when I sat down to catch my breath, it was warm.
